papers.title: Neutrophil-derived apoptotic bodies function as decoy signals to preserve bone integrity during infectious osteomyelitis.
papers.summary: In infected bone marrow, dying neutrophils release apoptotic bodies (neut-ABs) whose α2,3-sialylated TLR2 acts as a molecular decoy, competing with Siglec15-TLR2 interactions on osteoclast precursors to block fusion and bone resorption. Therapeutic delivery of neut-ABs attenuated osteolysis in infected mice without altering bacterial clearance, revealing an innate-immune-cell-to-bone signaling axis.

papers.title: Inhibition of cyclin-dependent kinase 8 modulates chondrocyte transition to hypertrophy and provides in vivo protection against spontaneous osteoarthritis.
papers.summary: CDK8/19 inhibitor treatment of a chemical library screen modulated chondrocyte behavior: it raised pro-anabolic/anti-catabolic markers, reduced hypertrophy and IL-1β-driven matrix degradation, and in STR/ort mice corrected gait, lowered serum OA biomarkers and limited mineralized growth-plate bridges. CDK8, MED12 and pSTAT1 co-localized in human OA lesions. Positioned as a disease-modifying osteoarthritis strategy.

papers.title: LMNA R527C pathogenic variant causes an inflammation-driven segmental progeroid syndrome via triggering DNA-sensing pathways.
papers.summary: The homozygous LMNA R527C variant produces an atypical, inflammation-driven segmental progeroid syndrome with autoimmune features. MSCs from affected individuals show inflammation and senescence; in mice it triggers chronic interferon signaling, thymic lymphomas after irradiation, and cGAS-STING hyperactivation via disrupted lamin A-DNA binding. Blocking DNA-sensing pathways suppressed inflammation, rescued senescence, and alleviated premature aging—a promising therapeutic target.

papers.title: Arrestins as programmable integrators of GPCR signaling: structural microstates, spatiotemporal logic, and therapeutic control.
papers.summary: Review synthesizing cryo-EM advances showing arrestins as programmable GPCR-signaling integrators rather than binary off-switches. Multiple engagement modes (core-, tail-, loop-, side-, membrane-anchored) are governed by phosphorylation barcodes, membrane cofactors, and isoform mechanics. Emerging therapeutic approaches include intracellular allosteric modulators and molecular glues that directly sculpt transducer assemblies, informing structure-guided GPCR drug design.

papers.title: Paratenial thalamus engages in reciprocal and broadcast circuits with the prefrontal cortex.
papers.summary: Using molecular profiling, tracing, electrophysiology and optogenetics, the paratenial thalamus (PT) is established as distinct from the paraventricular nucleus, labeled selectively by PKCδ. PT thalamocortical cells project to infralimbic mPFC L2/3 pyramidal cells; mPFC inputs are even stronger onto PT thalamostriatal/thalamoamygdala cells, enabling mPFC to broadcast to the subcortex. Parcellates the anterior midline thalamus and shows reciprocal subcortical throughput.

papers.title: Myosin1D directs circumferential F-actin flow to define cell chirality.
papers.summary: In Drosophila macrophages, Myosin1D directs clockwise and Myosin1C counterclockwise circumferential F-actin flow with Myosin2. In vitro, Myo1D self-organizes F-actin rings with aligned barbed-end polarity that rotate clockwise (Myo1C only induces random flow). Proposes that Myo1D assembles polarized F-actin arrays rotated clockwise by Myosin2, providing a molecular basis for cell and organ chirality.

papers.title: Cell cycle-dependent translation-mediated turnover of the long noncoding RNA Malat1.
papers.summary: Upon mitotic exit, the nuclear lncRNA Malat1 relocalizes to the cytoplasm and is degraded in early G1 via a translation- and SMG1-dependent decay pathway, resetting its abundance each cycle. Inhibiting decay or blocking mitotic progression leads to Malat1 accumulation, implicating a translation-harnessing, cell-cycle-gated mechanism and linking cancer-cell dormancy to Malat1 overexpression in cancer.

papers.title: An ancient alpharetrovirus lineage in bats: Evolutionary insights and possible roles in reproduction.
papers.summary: Paleovirological screening of 818 vertebrate genomes identified chiralphaenv, an alpharetrovirus lineage from cross-class saurian transmission. Bat genomes independently co-opted its envelope genes on eight occasions (43.8–18.9 Mya), maintained under purifying selection, with high endometrial expression in Carollia perspicillata suggesting reproductive function. Extends alpharetrovirus origins beyond 43 Mya and proposes the first mammalian co-opted alpharetrovirus-derived ERV in hemochorial placentation.

papers.title: Genomic characterization of historical Jinlingnan individuals: insights into genetic continuity and trans-Eurasian signals in eastern China.
papers.summary: Genome-wide SNP data from 10 Jinlingnan (Zibo, Shandong) individuals spanning Tang to Qing dynasties show primary ancestry from the middle Yellow River with strong genetic continuity to modern northern Chinese. Seven individuals carry 1.5–12.1% western-Eurasian/Central-Asian contributions, direct evidence of trans-Eurasian gene flow reaching inland eastern China; modern Shandong Han derive ~95% ancestry from a Jinlingnan-related source.

papers.title: Cell adhesion molecules CadN, DIP-α and klg regulate axon targeting and dendritic elaboration through synergistic and opposing effects.
papers.summary: In Drosophila lamina amacrine DM12 neurons, CadN and DIP-α cooperate in parallel to promote layer-specific axon targeting and dendritic elaboration; simultaneous loss worsens defects. Klg loss triggers dendritic-field expansion that scales total synapse number at constant density. Klg manipulation suppresses axon-mistargeting in DIP-α/CadN mutants, while DIP-α or CadN loss blunts Klg-driven expansion—showing opposing CAM roles fine-tune neurite morphogenesis.

papers.title: Autophagy, the Ubiquitin proteasome system, and the MAPK pathway control the temperature dependence of synaptic growth.
papers.summary: Using the Drosophila larval NMJ, tonic 1b bouton number is temperature-insensitive, but phasic 1s terminal growth increases with rearing temperature. This temperature-dependent growth requires autophagy, which itself varies with temperature, and is regulated through Highwire and a MAPK pathway. Wnd/MapKKK and p38b direct additional synaptic growth between 25°C and 29°C, showing temperature effects are neuron-specific and genetically regulated.

papers.title: Branched actin segregates endocytic cargo to control sorting and fission.
papers.summary: At the early endosome, Arp2/3-mediated branched (not formin linear) actin is required for fission and receptor recycling. Using Rab5-Q79L enlarged endosomes, recycling transferrin localized adjacent to branched actin; Arp2/3 inhibition dispersed cargo, coalescing clathrin-dependent degradative cargo with clathrin-independent recycling cargo, displacing receptors to the endosome. Identifies branched actin as a key regulator of cargo segregation, subdomain maintenance and fission.

papers.title: De novo assembly of the Trypanosoma congolense genome reveals an organisation influenced by antigenic variation but distinct from Trypanosoma brucei.
papers.summary: Long-read + Hi-C sequencing produced a telomere-to-telomere assembly of Trypanosoma congolense: 12 diploid chromosomes, one tetraploid and >100 small chromosomes. About 1500 VSG archive genes sit in smaller subtelomeres than in T. brucei with no dedicated expression site; one largely silent chromosome holds ~40% of the archive, a likely reservoir of new VSG variants.

papers.title: BIN1 overexpression rescues cardiac but not skeletal muscle defects in a mouse model of caveolinopathy.
papers.summary: In caveolin-3 knockout mice (caveolinopathy model), BIN1 overexpression failed to rescue skeletal muscle weakness, T-tubule structure or fiber atrophy but corrected nuclear positioning and partly restored mitochondrial markers. Conversely, it robustly rescued cardiac function—restoring end-diastolic volume, cardiac output and sarcomeric integrity. Tissue-specific dysregulation (including cavin-4) explains the differential rescue, supporting BIN1 as a candidate target for inherited cardiomyopathies.

papers.title: PES-8, a ZP-like protein, is required for cytoskeletal organization and contractility in the Caenorhabditis elegans spermatheca.
papers.summary: PES-8, a previously uncharacterized protein with an extracellular ZP-like domain and unstructured cytoplasmic tail, localizes to the C. elegans spermatheca plasma membrane. Its loss disrupts actomyosin fiber alignment, FLN-1/filamin localization, apical junction organization and Ca2+ signaling, preventing oocyte transit. Identifies PES-8 as a key regulator of cytoskeletal organization and calcium-mediated contractility in the spermatheca.

papers.title: Guarding the integrity of cell-based research: the role of the ICLAC Register of Misidentified Cell Lines.
papers.summary: Perspective on the ICLAC Register of Misidentified Cell Lines, whose Version 14 expands and updates entries on cell lines that do not match their claimed origin. The piece urges investigators to consult the register before acquiring lines, authenticate cultures at defined checkpoints (receipt, master stock, passaging, pre-publication) and report authentication evidence transparently, to curb cross-contamination and irreproducible cell-based research.

papers.title: Tet Trim-Away: a conditional rapid protein degradation system for Tetrahymena thermophila.
papers.summary: Tet Trim-Away adapts the TRIM21-based Trim-Away system for Tetrahymena thermophila, fusing TRIM21 RBCC domains with an α-mCherry nanobody that targets endogenously mCherry-tagged proteins for proteasome degradation. Driven by an inducible promoter, it depletes targets within ~30 min, is reversible, works across cellular compartments, and produces loss-of-function phenotypes—enabling rapid, acute protein-depletion studies beyond slow knockouts.

papers.title: Adventures through wonderland: the wild world of histone gene organization, evolution, and regulation in over 250 species.
papers.summary: Comprehensive curation catalogs and categorizes histone gene organizations across >250 species spanning 11 phyla, despite highly conserved histone protein sequence and S-phase-linked expression. Reveals divergent organizational themes even among closely related species alongside shared patterns in distant ones, proposes organization may influence gene regulation, and suggests misregulation of histone organization could contribute to disease.

papers.title: A role for the Stentor syntaxin protein in post-wound cell survival.
papers.summary: A targeted RNAi screen plus microfluidic-guillotine bisection in Stentor coeruleus identified a syntaxin gene essential for post-wound survival: only ~37% of syntaxin-deficient cells survived vs ~98% of controls. Knockdown cells were more vacuolated and sensitive to hypoosmotic shock, dying hours after wounding; wounding in 75 mM sorbitol partially restored survival. Implicates defective membrane fusion and osmotic-homeostasis machinery in wound healing.

papers.title: Kinesin-3 KIF1A functions as a diligent worker and its functionality is regulated by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
papers.summary: Live-cell imaging of iNeurons shows KIF1A fluorescence on axonal particles stays constant during transport, consistent with a 'diligent worker' that remains cargo-attached for the whole journey and is degraded at the end (short half-life). Inhibiting the ubiquitin/proteasome system halts KIF1A transport, produces cell-body aggregates cleared by aggrephagy—linking KIF1A turnover to proteostatic-stress signaling.

papers.title: Integrative chemical genetics platform identifies condensate modulators linked to neurological disorders.
papers.summary: CondensScreen integrates high-content screening with bioinformatics to find biomolecular-condensate modulators. Screening 1760 compounds in a DYT1 dystonia model identified drugs preventing MLF2 reporter accumulation in nuclear envelope condensates; a genome-wide CRISPR screen correlated condensate abundance with microcephaly and >8 neurodevelopmental-disorder genes. RNF26 deletion phenocopies torsin-deficiency hallmarks. A scalable platform linking condensate dysregulation to neurodevelopmental disease.

papers.title: Novel KIF22 variants disrupt mitosis in human chondrocytes and expand SEMDJL2 mechanisms.
papers.summary: Functional analysis of KIF22 variants in human chondrocytes: novel dominant p.P144T and p.E222Q retain polar-ejection-force activity; recessive R49Q shows reduced force. Live imaging shows all perturb mitosis—heterozygous variants impede anaphase segregation and spindle-pole separation (constitutive activation failing to inactivate at anaphase onset), while R49Q gives milder, partially penetrant defects. Expands SEMDJL2 mechanism to two classes of KIF22 dysregulation.

papers.title: Pre-clinical efficacy of a C4BP hexameric IgG Fc fusion protein against Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
papers.summary: A C4BP domain 1+2 fragment fused to hexameric IgG Fc (C4BP-hexa IgG Fc) showed ~650-fold greater complement-dependent bactericidal activity than monomeric C4BP-IgG1 Fc against Neisseria gonorrhoeae, enhanced neutrophil uptake, and—despite off-target complement activation—reduced duration and burden of vaginal colonization in human FH/C4BP transgenic mice. Proof-of-concept against this multidrug-resistant pathogen.

papers.title: Transcriptome analysis of hepatopancreas of Litopenaeus vannamei after acute exposure to Alexandrium pacificum.
papers.summary: Litopenaeus vannamei shrimp were immersed in Alexandrium pacificum lysate; hepatopancreas transcriptomics at 72 h identified 264 DEGs (185 up, 79 down), enriched in signal transduction, oxidative phosphorylation, lysosome, C-type lectin receptor signaling, peroxisome and drug metabolism. Provides molecular insight into the shrimp's immune and metabolic defenses against this red-tide dinoflagellate toxin.

papers.title: First complete genome sequences and transcript expression profiling of tea plant necrotic ring blotch virus isolates from Iran.
papers.summary: High-throughput sequencing yielded the first complete genome sequences of two Iranian tea plant necrotic ring blotch virus (TPNRBV) isolates. Transcript profiling showed elevated p22 (then p24, p14) ORF expression; 93 SNPs concentrate in RNA1/RNA2. Iranian isolates cluster phylogenetically with Chinese isolates. p22's role is unknown but elevated expression warrants investigation; amino-acid-changing SNPs point to evolutionary/pathogenicity significance.

papers.title: Mutation-driven structural and functional changes in ACE2 and their potential implications for Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: In silico framework assessed ACE2 missense SNPs for Alzheimer's-disease relevance. Multi-tier screening (SIFT, PANTHER, PhD-SNP, SNPs&GO, FoldX, DynaMut2, MCSM) plus MD simulations showed variants F308S, L186S, Y654S and L570S destabilize ACE2—increased backbone deviation, flexibility, solvent exposure, reduced compactness and weakened angiotensin-II docking; L570S was most severe. Provides mechanistic basis for ACE2 polymorphisms contributing to AD.

papers.title: Postoperative wound microenvironment regulates breast cancer stem cell fate and clinical implications.
papers.summary: Review of the postoperative wound-healing niche in breast cancer: wound fluid contains inflammatory cytokines/growth factors (partly modulated by intraoperative radiotherapy) that can induce cancer-stem-cell phenotypes, self-renewal and EMT via inflammation/JAK-STAT networks, linked to recurrence and resistance. Wound fluid is a candidate biomarker source, though current evidence rests largely on in vitro/surrogate models; spatial multi-omics and 3D models are proposed.

papers.title: Enhanced mitochondrial fission promotes chemosensitivity via SHP-1 activity in triple-negative breast cancer.
papers.summary: In SUM149/SUM159 TNBC cells, enhanced mitochondrial fission (via PISD/DRP1) increased sensitivity to doxorubicin and salinomycin (not paclitaxel), an effect attenuated by SHP-1/2 inhibition and specifically by SHP-1 knockdown; fusion conferred resistance. Identifies SHP-1 as a key regulator linking mitochondrial dynamics to chemosensitivity, a potential pathway for overcoming TNBC chemoresistance.

papers.title: Microbiome and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: mechanistic insights, microenvironmental interactions, and therapeutic implications.
papers.summary: Review of microbiome–PDAC interplay: dysbiosis spans gut, oral and intratumoral microbial communities, with Firmicutes-associated taxa notable for SCFA production and immunometabolic effects. Microbiota-derived metabolites show context-dependent tumor-promoting or -suppressive roles in immune remodeling and the TME; microbial signatures/metabolites are explored as biomarkers, and microbiome-modulating strategies (prebiotics, FMT, metabolite interventions) may influence therapy response, though evidence remains largely preclinical.

papers.title: The dual role of AMPK in cancer metabolic reprogramming.
papers.summary: Review of AMPK's dual role in cancer metabolic reprogramming: initially seen as a tumor suppressor via LKB1-linked growth suppression, recent evidence shows pro-survival, tumor-promoting activity under hypoxia, nutrient deprivation and oxidative stress. Summarizes AMPK as central to glucose/lipid/amino-acid metabolism and autophagy regulation, catalogs AMPK-targeted therapeutic strategies, and discusses challenges and future directions in AMPK-based metabolic cancer therapy.

papers.title: IL-1β-induced inflammatory stress modulates mitochondrial and metabolic gene expression in dermal fibroblasts.
papers.summary: In an in vitro model, IL-1β (10 ng/ml) treatment of human dermal fibroblasts altered mitochondrial-homeostasis gene expression: increased SOD2 (oxidative stress) with reduced CS, ACSL1 and TOMM20 (impaired lipid metabolism/mitochondrial integrity), alongside decreased viability, lower ATP, higher ROS and inflammation-associated morphology. In silico analyses confirmed the target genes, establishing a reliable IL-1β-based inflammatory model for studying mitochondrial dysfunction.

papers.title: Molecular cartography of breast cancer: decoding genomes, heterogeneity and the tumor microenvironment for personalized targeted therapeutics.
papers.summary: Review dissecting breast-cancer molecular complexity: discusses gene mutations in pathogenesis, tumor heterogeneity and hormone-receptor pathways underlying variable presentation, the tumor microenvironment and the dual protective/promoting roles of immune cells and immune-evasion tactics. Provides a molecular background informing current targeted-therapy improvements, with illustrative figures clarifying the underlying mechanisms.

papers.title: Optimization of a Canine Colon Organoid Platform for Modeling Intestinal Injury and Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Mediated Regeneration.
papers.summary: Optimized canine colon organoid (CCO) platform: Wnt/EGF activation plus TGF-β/p38 MAPK inhibition sustains stem-cell-enriched organoids; maturation yields absorptive and secretory cells with functional P-gp efflux. Diclofenac injury is more pronounced in differentiated organoids, recapitulating cell-type-specific sensitivity. MSC-conditioned medium induces fetal-like regenerative spheroids and restores growth/barrier integrity in injured organoids, supporting modeling of intestinal injury and repair.

papers.title: The regulatory network of Salmonella biofilm formation: the role of CsgD on autoinducer-2 activity and expression of quorum-sensing-related genes in Salmonella Typhimurium.
papers.summary: Modulating CsgD in Salmonella Typhimurium altered quorum-sensing-linked sRNA expression (MicA, CsrB, CsrC, RyeE) and AI-2 signaling: CsgD overexpression raised relative AI-2 activity 277% with increased LsrK expression; CsgD loss upregulated LsrA/LsrK/LsrR while AI-2 stayed flat, suggesting inhibitory LsrR is counterbalanced by increased LsrA/LsrK. CsgD deletion reduced curli/cellulose biofilm phenotypes, positioning CsgD as an integrative node bridging biofilm regulation and quorum sensing.

papers.title: The genome-wide analysis of the NAC gene family in Pseudoroegneria libanotica highlights the functions of PlNAC17/20 under abiotic stress conditions.
papers.summary: First genome-wide analysis of the NAC family in Pseudoroegneria libanotica: 217 NAC genes in 11 subfamilies; syntenic conservation is stronger with wheat than Arabidopsis, with dispersed duplication driving expansion under purifying selection. Transcriptomics identified 14 drought-responsive PlNAC genes, notably PlNAC17/20; co-expression and yeast assays support stress-responsive functions, informing NAC-mediated stress tolerance improvement in Triticeae crops.

papers.title: HOXC9 transcriptionally activates NRP1 to promote cell malignant progression and immune evasion in colorectal cancer.
papers.summary: In colorectal cancer, HOXC9 is upregulated and predicts poor prognosis. Silencing it suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, stemness and PD-L1 expression, enhanced CD8+ T-cell function, and reduced tumor growth in xenografts. HOXC9 transcriptionally activates NRP1; NRP1 overexpression reverses HOXC9-knockdown effects. Elucidates a HOXC9→NRP1 axis driving malignant progression and immune evasion in CRC.
